title: Beyond Hate Speech: NLP’s Challenges and Opportunities in Uncovering Dehumanizing Language

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing F1 scores, false positive rates (over-sensitivity), and false negative rates (recognition blindness) in dehumanization detection across racial and ethnic target groups (e.g., Black people, South Asians, Arabs, Chinese people, Mixed race).
Evaluating classification disparities, including F1 scores and error rates, for dehumanizing language targeting religious groups such as Muslims and Jewish people.
Measuring over-sensitivity (predicting dehumanization on non-dehumanizing hate speech) and recognition blindness in model predictions for groups like Gay men and Lesbians.
Assessing model performance disparities and error patterns in identifying dehumanization targeting Women.
Evaluating F1 scores and misclassification rates (over-sensitivity/recognition blindness) for dehumanization detection targeting Trans people.
Measuring recognition blindness (false negative ratios) when detecting dehumanizing language directed at Refugees and Immigrants.
Analyzing dehumanization classification performance and error disparities for language targeting the Working Class.
Evaluating dehumanization detection performance and error rates targeting People with disabilities.
